title: Synthetic transport-encryption calibration
prompt: A fictional lab team uses key agreement and AES-GCM but skips all peer-identity checks and repeats the same key/nonce pair. A manager says encryption alone proves the intended remote supplier identity. Evaluate the claim and propose authorized checks.
initialDirections: Explain agreement versus authentication, assess the manager claim and intermediary risk, explain GCM nonce reuse, propose identity and local encryption checks, and state scope and limits.
replyDirections: Address a specific peer claim or the independent claim with a justified correction or check.
alternate: Independent claim: a successful local encryption test proves the remote supplier identity.
gradingInstructions: Key agreement establishes shared material; authentication verifies the intended peer. Encryption by itself does not verify that peer. An active intermediary can create separate encrypted sessions. GCM nonces must be unique under a given key; reuse can undermine confidentiality and authentication. Expected-name/certificate-chain/handshake verification addresses identity. Authorized isolated synthetic-data checks can test byte recovery and altered-ciphertext rejection. Local success does not prove remote identity or whole-protocol security. Incorrect, absent or merely repeated vocabulary is not supporting evidence.

criteria.label: Agreement and identity
criteria.description: Explain shared secrets, intended identity, the unsupported claim and intermediary risk.
evidenceChecks: Explains that key agreement establishes shared secret material.
Explains that peer authentication verifies the intended party.
Rejects the claim that encryption alone proves the intended peer identity.
Explains a concrete impostor or intermediary risk when identity checks are absent.

criteria.label: Nonce and proposed checks
criteria.description: Explain GCM reuse risks and uniqueness, then propose identity and safe encryption checks.
evidenceChecks: Explains that repeating a GCM key/nonce pair can break confidentiality or authentication.
Requires nonce uniqueness for each encryption under a GCM key without claiming nonce secrecy.
Proposes checking the authenticated expected peer identity, beyond merely decrypting.
Proposes a concrete safe local encryption check, such as byte-for-byte recovery or rejecting altered ciphertext.

criteria.label: Scenario reasoning
criteria.description: Connect two supplied facts to the risk or recommendation.
evidenceChecks: Uses the missing identity checks as evidence for the conclusion.
Uses another supplied fact, such as the manager claim or repeated key/nonce, to justify a conclusion.
Explains how a supplied fact causes a risk or motivates a recommendation.

criteria.label: Scope and limits
criteria.description: Distinguish local checks from remote identity and propose authorized isolated testing.
evidenceChecks: Explains that a local encryption check does not establish remote peer identity or complete protocol security.
Scopes proposed tests to authorized isolated work with synthetic data or supplied records.

criteria.label: Independent reply
criteria.description: Address the independent claim with a justified check, correction or limitation.
evidenceChecks: Addresses the specific peer or independent claim in the writer own response.
Uses an accurate relevant concept or scenario fact in that response.
Adds an accurate specific check, correction or limit beyond agreement.
Explains why the addition matters to the claim.
